title: SSC Spot the Error - Practice by Parts of Speech
description: Grammar error-spotting practice questions from SSC CGL/CHSL/MTS/CPO/Stenographer exams, categorized by part of speech / grammar concept.

questions.sentence: The committee has postponed 1 the announcement until 2 further informations is received 3 from the regional offices. 4
questions.explanation: Information is an uncountable noun and has no plural form.

questions.sentence: A large number of equipments were delivered to the warehouse 1 last week 2 to support the upcoming production schedule 3 without any delay. 4
questions.explanation: Equipment is an uncountable noun; it has no plural form 'equipments'.

questions.sentence: The manager distributed 1 many important informations 2 during the morning briefing, 3 causing some confusion. 4
questions.explanation: Information is uncountable; use 'pieces of information' instead of 'informations'.

questions.sentence: He had never seen 1 such a masterpiece 2 until he 3 visits the gallery last spring. 4
questions.explanation: The action happened in the past, so the past tense verb 'visited' is required, not present tense 'visits'.

questions.sentence: They enjoyed 1 the sceneries 2 during their trip 3 to the mountains 4.
questions.explanation: Scenery is an uncountable noun and does not take a plural 's'.

questions.sentence: The news are 1 quite surprising 2 and hard to believe 3 for the public 4.
questions.explanation: 'News' is grammatically singular although it ends in 's'; hence it takes a singular verb 'is'.

questions.sentence: Had he been knowing 1 about the regulatory changes 2 he would not have proceeded 3 with the merger deal. 4
questions.explanation: Third conditional structure requires 'had + V3', not 'had been knowing'.

questions.explanation: 'Two of the world's best forwards' is a plural subject and requires the plural verb 'have'.

questions.sentence: These pieces of equipments are handled by trained technicians.
questions.explanation: Equipment, furniture, jewellery, scenery, poetry are always singular/uncountable and never take a plural 's'.

questions.sentence: I want to spend some quiet moments in the forest passing with trees and enjoy the peaceful natural scenery.
